Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary (≤500 words)

Overview
The Conservatives present themselves as guardians of Britain’s economic revival since 1979 and argue for continuity: low taxes, limited government, pro-enterprise reform, constitutional stability, and a strong, sovereign UK in a flexible Europe. They contrast this with what they describe as Labour’s higher-cost “social model.”

Economy and Jobs
- Keep public spending growing more slowly than the economy; aim for government spending under 40% of GDP, move toward a balanced budget by 2000.
- Target a 20p basic income tax rate and retain a 40p top rate; keep Britain as the lowest-tax major European economy.
- Maintain 2.5% inflation target; protect low mortgage rates.
- Oppose the EU Social Chapter, Working Time Directive application to the UK, and a national minimum wage.
- Cut burdens on business, expand deregulation with “sunset” clauses, reform business rates to favor small firms, and further reduce capital gains and inheritance taxes when prudent.
- Expand welfare-to-work: extend Project Work nationally for long-term unemployed; create “Britain Works” partnerships.

Ownership, Families, Welfare
- Transfer unused personal tax allowance to a working spouse for families with dependent children/relatives (worth up to £17.50/week).
- Promote saving and share ownership (Share Match for employees); continue raising inheritance tax thresholds pragmatically.
- Pensions: introduce personal pension funds for new entrants to the workforce via NI rebates, guaranteed at least the current basic state pension; older workers unaffected.
- Social services reform for greater accountability, standards across sectors, more choice (vouchers/direct payments), respite care for carers, and a partnership model for long-term elderly care.
- Protect Child Benefit and Family Credit; intensify anti-fraud measures.

Education
- “Education Guarantee”: rigorous testing (ages 5, 7, 11, 14; publish results), tougher standards in literacy/numeracy, stricter exams, strong inspections, intervention in failing schools/LEAs, teacher appraisal tied to pupil outcomes, strengthened discipline and RE.
- Choice/diversity: more specialist schools, selective admissions by aptitude, support grammar schools where parents want them, expand Assisted Places, maintain nursery vouchers for all 4-year-olds.
- Post-16: learning credits (14–21), National Traineeships, expand Modern Apprenticeships; uphold world-class university research pending Dearing.

Health and Public Services
- NHS: real-terms increases each year; shorter waits; expand GP fundholding and primary care services (including nurse prescribing); invest via Private Finance Initiative (PFI); strengthen mental health care; prevention through “Health of the Nation.”
- Public services: extend Citizens’ Charter; expand PFI; continue privatisation and competition (complete rail, privatise London Underground and National Air Traffic Services; reform Post Office/Royal Mail while protecting universal service).

Law and Order
- More police recruitment; expand CCTV (10,000 cameras target); voluntary ID card via photo driving licence.
- Juvenile crime: parental control orders, reparation, curfews with electronic monitoring, secure training for persistent offenders.
- National Crime Squad; mandatory minimum sentences (repeat serious violent/sexual offences = automatic life; persistent burglars = 3 years; hard drug dealers = 7 years); end automatic early release; stronger victim protections.
- Legal aid within cash limits; faster criminal justice.

Society, Places, Environment
- Regenerate worst estates via tenant-led stock transfer/private capital (~£25bn over a decade); extend Rough Sleepers Initiative nationally; protect green belt; target 60% of new homes on brownfield; support rural services and jobs; no general right to roam.
- Agriculture/fisheries: robust BSE response; independent food safety leadership; CAP reform; defend quotas/limits; raise animal welfare standards EU-wide.
- Lead on environment (air/water quality, “polluter pays”).
- Expand arts, sport, and youth talent via National Lottery.

Europe, Foreign Policy, Defence, Constitution
- Europe: partnership of nation states; retain veto, rebate, border controls; oppose federalism and Social Chapter; push enlargement and single market reform.
- Single currency: keep options open; unlikely by 1999; any UK entry only after a referendum.
- Defence: stable funding, rapid deployment capability, NATO central; no defence review.
- Constitution: evolutionary reform, more open government and better Parliamentary scrutiny; oppose PR, a new Bill of Rights, and devolution to Scottish/Welsh assemblies; uphold the Union; negotiate for peace in Northern Ireland under consent principle.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a fair, free, open society by widening opportunity, spreading power, and balancing liberty, equality and community. Active government should invest in people, safeguard security, protect the environment and be answerable to citizens.

Education (flagship): Extra £2bn/year funded by +1p on the basic income tax rate.
- Early years: High‑quality education for all 3–4 year‑olds.
- Schools: Double spending on books/equipment in year one; cut primary classes to max 30 within 5 years; £500m over 5 years to fix buildings; strengthen teaching via a General Teaching Council; focused Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; literacy drive; tougher inspection including LEAs; discipline, anti‑bullying and truancy action.
- School governance: More parental/community roles; more school autonomy under “light touch” LEAs; end selection by local choice; integrate GM schools/CTCs.
- Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based system post‑14; universal IT access; 2% remissible training levy (SMEs exempt); raise 16–19 training; Quality Council for post‑16; protect research/academic freedom.

Economy and jobs:
- Stability: Independent Bank of England; keep the “golden rule” (borrow only to invest); promote PPPs; consider euro entry if Maastricht criteria met, UK meets them, and referendum approves.
- Skills and work: Convert long‑term unemployment benefits into “working benefits”; invest in training; remove poverty traps.
- Enterprise/SMEs: Late‑payment interest right; cut red tape; expand seed capital; regional Development Agencies; shift R&D from military to civil; promote tourism; employee participation and profit‑sharing; stronger shareholder say.
- Competition/consumers/utilities: Stronger competition law; unified utility regulator; independent financial services regulation; better redress and labelling (incl. GM foods).

Environment and transport:
- Tax shift from jobs/VAT to pollution (no net rise); new quality‑of‑life indicators; 30% CO2 cut from 1990 within 15 years.
- Public transport: Urban road pricing to fund clean transit; London Underground public; treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010; stricter Railtrack targets with power to re‑acquire control if persistently failing.
- Motoring: Cut small‑car VED to £10, offset by ~4p/litre fuel duty; greener company car rules.
- Energy/homes: National insulation for 2m lowest‑income households; phased carbon tax offset by cuts to VAT/employers’ NI; higher efficiency standards; boost renewables; no new nuclear subsidies; manage waste safely.
- Countryside/water/wildlife: Stronger protections; target leakage; fairer water charging with profit‑sharing; green farming via Countryside Management Contracts; prefer brownfield; animal welfare upgrades; free vote on hunting.

Safer, stronger communities:
- 3,000 more police on the beat; faster, smarter justice; restorative justice/youth focus; local crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support.
- Housing: Build more via partnerships; release council‑house receipts; Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers (new borrowers), moving toward unified housing cost relief; end rough sleeping by 2000; tenant rights; tackle empty homes; fairer rules for under‑25s.

NHS and care:
- +£540m/year (funded by closing NI loopholes and +5p per cigarette pack); halt finance‑driven closures for 6 months; recruit frontline staff (e.g., 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors); max 6‑month waits within 3 years; end two‑tier GP system; National Inspectorate; free eye/dental checks; shift to prevention; stronger patient rights; more open, locally accountable trusts; better community care and a new Carer’s Benefit.

Constitutional reform:
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law); Human Rights Commission; Freedom of Information; cut quangos; referendums on major constitutional change.
- Parliament: PR for all elections; reduce MPs by 200; reformed (mainly elected) second chamber; fixed 4‑year terms; party finance transparency/limits.
- Devolution: Home Rule for Scotland and Wales (PR, tax‑varying powers); elected English regional assemblies where desired; stronger local government; long‑term Local Income Tax/business rate reform.
- Northern Ireland: Power‑sharing under PR; civil liberties safeguards; fair policing/justice reforms; support peace within Mitchell principles.

Opportunity and equality:
- Tax/benefits: Raise personal allowance by £200 and create a 50% rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a simpler Low Income Benefit; crackdown on fraud/evasion.
- Work and families: National childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; flexible parental leave/benefit; reform child support via unified family courts.
- Older people: Earnings‑linked top‑up to guarantee minimum income; flexible retirement 60–70; outlaw age discrimination; move from SERPS to secure, portable personal/occupational pensions; abolish water standing charges.
- Women, disabled, minorities, LGBT: Stronger equal rights and anti‑discrimination laws; better access/services; equal age of consent; repeal Section 28; tackle hate crime.

Foreign policy, defence, development:
- Pro‑European leadership; more accountable EU; PR for 1999 MEPs; support euro with conditions/referendum; CAP/CFP reform (regional fisheries management).
- Defence: Maintain current capability; keep Trident (fewer warheads); support NATO/enlargement; push CTBT.
- UN/international law: Stronger UN peacekeeping; International Criminal Court; global environmental governance; aid to 0.7% GNP within 10 years; debt relief; end arms sales to abusers; ban landmines; fair trade with labour and environmental standards.

Tax contract: Transparency, costing with prices, waste‑cutting first, and fair burden sharing; about 70% of adults pay lower or unchanged income tax; average taxpayer (excluding >£100k) pays ~45p/week more.
